meaning: Answer map for Q-MORAL-GROUNDING (what makes something objectively good or evil?). O'Connor's emotivism: no objective grounding; moral statements have no truth value (OCONNOR-DESTINY-ETHICS-EMOTIVISM; in 2016, no objective moral truths, OCONNOR-TUREK-EVIL-NO-OBJECTIVE-MORAL-TRUTHS). Catholic theory: goodness is the same in reality as being in act (ST I q.5 a.1); evil is the privation of a due good (q.48 a.3), and 'there is evil' is true when such a privation is in a subject (q.48 a.2 ad 2). Naturalist moral realism: unexplained for now; no pinnable proponent text, recorded as candidate NATURALIST-MORAL-REALISM-RAILTON. Verified coverage cells for the evidence item 'the evil premise is true', under the shared background: entailed by the Catholic theory, contradicted by emotivism. The Comparator config also verifies that emotivism is consistent with the background, so the contradiction is with the evil premise and not with the background. Proof shape: each cell is a short derivation (Catholic: deficiency, privation, then propositional truth; emotivism: the same three steps as POE-EXTERNAL-PREMISE-VS-EMOTIVISM). No premise already states a cell.
